subject: Post-call: Reservation governance, isolation needs & scaling checklist (MedSonic)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Yang <claire@medsonic.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — reserved pool sizing, isolation, SLAs

Hi Claire — thanks again for the time earlier today. Short recap from our side and a few items we promised to follow up on. Please flag anything we missed.

1) Pain points you confirmed
- Production latency spikes during batch ingest windows (95th pct > 1.2s for conversational inference).
- Regulatory requirement for logical isolation of PHI workloads (separate GPU pool + VPC egress controls).
- Cost predictability: need a committed monthly spend cap and clear burst behavior.

2) Goals you shared
- Deploy clinical summarization and triage models (LLM seq len ~1k tokens) with steady throughput of ~120 qps during peak.
- SLO: p95 latency <= 800ms for online requests, availability SLO 99.9% for reserved pool.
- Data handling: logs/audit retention 13 months, KMS-managed keys.

3) Redwood proposal highlights we agreed to explore
- Reserved GPU pool (dedicated tenancy) sized for steady 120 qps with 30% headroom for spikes.
- Tenant isolation via dedicated pool + strict VPC peering and egress rules.
- Canary rollout with fallback to multi-tenant hosted endpoint for brief loss of capacity.
- Draft SLA template + commitment estimate (attached).

Action items — owners & tentative dates
- Redwood: provide an initial capacity estimate + cost workbook with burst scenarios (attachment: medsonic-commitment-estimate.xlsx) — Logan — by 2026-08-27.
- MedSonic: share procurement contact and any contract constraints/standard terms — Claire/Ravi — by 2026-08-28.
- Redwood Eng/Infra (Jordan & Marissa): validate isolation controls and KB checklist for PHI workloads (include KMS/HSM touchpoints) — Jordan/Marissa — internal by 2026-08-30.

Attachments: rdw-dedicated-sla-outline.pdf (draft SLA), medsonic-commitment-estimate.xlsx (working numbers).

If that matches your notes, I’ll turn this into a mutual action plan and schedule a short sync with procurement. Thanks — talk soon.

—
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
loganw@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

From: Claire Yang <claire@medsonic.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@medsonic.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 18:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — reserved pool sizing, isolation, SLAs

Thanks, Logan — this is great and aligns with what we covered. A couple clarifications: 

- The 120 qps is an expected steady state for the summarization service, but peak bursts can hit ~200 qps for short windows (2–5 minutes) after nightly batch ingestion. Please make sure the workbook models a short-duration burst profile.
- For PHI isolation we need proof points around egress controls and key separation (we use AWS KMS today). Can you call out whether HSM integration is available for on-prem keys?

Procurement: I’ve looped Ravi (cc). He’ll own the contract timeline and any standard redlines. Ravi — our goal is to understand committed capacity pricing vs. flexible burst add-on.

I’m available for a 30-minute follow-up Friday morning if you want to walk through the workbook.

—
Claire Yang
Head of Data Products, MedSonic Health
claire@medsonic.ai | +1 617-555-2244

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Yang <claire@medsonic.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@medsonic.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — reserved pool sizing, isolation, SLAs

Appreciate the clarifications, Claire. Quick notes against your questions: 

- Burst modeling: yes — the attached workbook includes a "burst profile" sheet that simulates 2–8 minute spikes to 200 qps and shows cost delta for three burst strategies (overprovisioned reserved pool, elastic burst credits, on-demand fallback). See medsonic-commitment-estimate.xlsx.
- HSM/KMS: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS keys; HSM-backed key stores depend on your provider (we can integrate with AWS CloudHSM or on-prem HSM via our Private deployment model). I’ve asked Jordan/Marissa to capture exact integration steps and an ops checklist.

Next steps (updated):
- Logan: finalize capacity workbook and call Friday 08/28 @ 10:00 AM ET to review with Ravi and Claire — I’ll send the invite.
- Jordan: produce an isolation controls runbook (network egress controls, VPC peering, KMS/HSM notes) — due internal draft 08/30, share to MedSonic by 09/02.
- Marissa: prepare a short ops acceptance checklist for canary rollback triggers (latency, error-rate thresholds) — due 08/30.

Ravi — can you confirm availability for Friday 10:00 AM ET? If that doesn’t work, we’ll propose alternatives.

Thanks — attaching an updated SLA outline with the p95 and availability targets called out.

Attachment: rdw-dedicated-sla-outline.pdf

—
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
loganw@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Claire Yang <claire@medsonic.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — reserved pool sizing, isolation, SLAs

Quick one-line confirm — I’ll take the isolation runbook and include: VPC peering template, security group minimums, KMS integration notes (AWS KMS + CloudHSM callouts), and recommended throughput headroom for 1k token seq lengths. Will share internal draft by 08/30.

If anyone has specific compliance artifacts (SOC2 report, encryption certs) they want included, list them and we’ll attach to the pack.

—
